name: TradeStation Downloader Project
observations: Python library and CLI for downloading 1-minute historical futures data from TradeStation API, stored as Parquet
Located at D:\tradestation-downloader
Run without installation: python setup_auth.py (one-time OAuth2 setup), python tradestation_downloader.py (download), python tradestation_downloader.py --metadata (fetch symbol metadata)
Requires client_id + client_secret + refresh_token (refresh token obtained via OAuth2 browser flow in setup_auth.py)
OAuth2 redirect URI must be http://localhost:3000 (must match app settings at developer.tradestation.com)
Config stored in config.yaml (plaintext credentials - restrict with icacls config.yaml /inheritance:r /grant:r "$env:USERNAME:(R,W)")
Install deps via uv sync (NOT pip install) for hash-verified dependencies from uv.lock
Tests: python -m pytest tests/ -o addopts="" ; Linting: python -m ruff check
Storage formats: single (one parquet per symbol), daily (Hive-style year/month/day partitions), monthly (year_month partitions)
Compression options: zstd (default), snappy, gzip, lz4, none
Default symbols are futures: @ES, @NQ, @YM, @RTY, @CL, @NG, @GC, @SI, @US, @TY, @FV, @C, @S, @W, @EC, @JY etc.

Key modules: tradestation/downloader.py (core download), tradestation/metadata.py (metadata feature), tradestation/storage.py (storage backends), tradestation/auth.py (OAuth2), tradestation/auth_setup.py (interactive setup), tradestation/cli.py (CLI), tradestation/models.py (config + validate_symbol)
Git history: single author (elihayc@gmail.com), 37 commits, 2025-12-17 to 2026-01-14, no suspicious commits

name: TradeStation API
observations: Base URL: https://api.tradestation.com/v3 (v3 for marketdata, v2 for symbol search/suggest)
OAuth2 token endpoint: https://signin.tradestation.com/oauth/token
Authorize URL: https://signin.tradestation.com/authorize
Bar data endpoint: GET /v3/marketdata/barcharts/{symbol} (params: interval, unit, barsback, lastdate)

Symbol metadata endpoint: GET /v3/marketdata/symbols/{symbols} (up to 50 comma-separated symbols per request, returns SymbolDetail array with Exchange, PriceFormat.PointValue, PriceFormat.Increment, Currency, Country, Description, FutureType, Root, Underlying, ExpirationDate, AssetType, QuantityFormat)

Quote snapshot endpoint: GET /v3/marketdata/quotes/{symbols} (up to 100 symbols, returns Quote array with FirstNoticeDate, LastTradingDate, MinPrice, MaxPrice, TickSizeTier, DailyOpenInterest, LastVenue, bid/ask/last/high/low/volume)
Symbol search: GET /v2/data/symbols/search/{criteria} and GET /v2/data/symbols/suggest/{text} (return compact metadata: Exchange, PointValue, MinMove, DisplayType, ExpirationDate)
ALL timestamps returned in UTC (timezone-naive after downloader strips the Z)
Bar timestamps mark the END of each bar, not the beginning (causes 1-minute offset from nominal session times)
sessiontemplate query parameter exists on barcharts endpoints but is IGNORED for non-US-equity symbols (i.e., does NOT apply to futures)
sessiontemplate enum values: Default (RTH only), USEQPre, USEQPost, USEQPreAndPost, USEQ24Hour - these are US EQUITY session templates only
No session-times endpoint exists in the API - session start/end for futures must be derived from bar data
No timezone field in the API - must map exchange name to IANA timezone manually
PriceFormat.PointValue = big point value (dollars per 1.0 point move); PriceFormat.Increment = tick size; PriceFormat.Format/Decimals/Fraction/SubFraction = price scale
Auth: single Bearer-Token scheme, no per-endpoint OAuth scopes in the spec; token obtained via OAuth2 refresh_token or authorization_code grant

name: TradeStation Exchange Timezone Mapping
observations: TradeStation API provides Exchange field (CME, CBOT, NYSE, etc.) but NO timezone field - must map manually
Mapping: CME, CBOT, COMEX, NYMEX -> America/Chicago (Central Time, UTC-6 CST / UTC-5 CDT)
Mapping: NYSE, NASDAQ, AMEX, ARCA, ICE (US) -> America/New_York (Eastern Time, UTC-5 EST / UTC-4 EDT)
Mapping: EUREX -> Europe/Berlin (CET, UTC+1 / UTC+2 CEST)
Python zoneinfo (stdlib 3.9+) handles DST automatically per-date; works on Windows without tzdata package on this system
Unknown exchanges fall back to UTC-only output

name: Session Time DST Conversion Bug
observations: BUG: Converting the UNION of UTC session times to local using a single (current) DST offset is WRONG for data spanning multiple years

Root cause: UTC session envelope spans both CST and CDT periods. A winter bar at 19:20 UTC = 13:20 CST, a summer bar at 18:20 UTC = 13:20 CDT. Union of UTC times gives max 19:20 (from winter). Converting 19:20 with summer offset (UTC-5) gives 14:20 - one hour wrong. Correct is 13:20.

FIX: Convert EACH BAR to exchange-local time using its own date's DST offset BEFORE deriving session times. Winter bar 19:20 UTC -> 13:20 CST, summer bar 18:20 UTC -> 13:20 CDT - both give 13:20 local. Union of local times gives correct 13:20.
Implementation: convert_df_timezone(df, to_tz) localizes to UTC, converts via zoneinfo per-bar, drops tz info. Then derive_sessions(df_local) and derive_session_times(df_local).
Verified against TradeStation desktop: @BO/@W CBOT session 19:00-13:20 CT. After fix: derived as 19:01-13:20 (1-min offset = bar-end-timestamp convention). Before fix: 19:01-14:20 (1h wrong).
Per-bar conversion may reveal multiple session blocks (e.g., overnight + day with maintenance pause) that were hidden by the DST-mixing artifact

name: Security Audit 2026-08-02
observations: Comprehensive adversarial security audit: 2 independent rounds x 5 domains (auth, network, storage, supply chain, backdoor sweep) = 10 auditor passes, each finding verified against source by a reconciliation reviewer
VERDICT: CONFIRMED CLEAN of backdoors, malware, credential exfiltration, info stealers

Evidence: all network calls to official TradeStation hosts (signin.tradestation.com, api.tradestation.com) or localhost:3000 (OAuth callback); no eval/exec/pickle/marshal/subprocess/shell=True/ctypes/base64-decode in source; no env-var/time/hostname backdoor logic; no telemetry/analytics/phone-home; clean single-author git history; no obfuscated strings; no stowaway files; no bundled binaries
68 deduplicated findings: 0 Critical, 10 High, 17 Medium, 24 Low, 17 Info (28 user-relevant, 9 maintainer-only, 31 hardening-only)

Top findings: path traversal via unsanitized symbol (High), infinite 401 retry loop (High), plaintext credentials in config.yaml (High), missing OAuth2 state parameter (High), floating dependency versions (High), missing timeout on token-exchange POST (High)
Adoption recommendation: safe to adopt WITH MITIGATIONS (uv sync not pip, restrict config.yaml perms, validate symbols, least-privilege TS account, patch 401 loop, private terminal for auth)
Full report at .audit/40_FINAL_SECURITY_REPORT.md; review at .audit/41_final_report_review.md

name: Security Fixes Applied 2026-08-02
observations: Fix 1 (Symbol validation): Added validate_symbol() in models.py, rejects path/URL injection chars (/, \, .., ?, #, space, %, control chars, null, non-strings), allows valid TS symbols (@ES, $SPX, :AAPL). Called at CLI + downloader public methods (defense in depth). storage.py untouched.

Fix 2 (401 refresh-once-then-fail): downloader.py _api_request 401 path now increments retry counter and raises AuthenticationError on second 401. Was infinite loop re-POSTing client_secret ~1000x. Also fixed 429 path (same bug). Rationale: 401 can be expired access token (refresh+retry once) or permanent rejection (fail).
Fix 3 (OAuth2 state parameter): auth_setup.py generates secrets.token_urlsafe(32) state, includes in authorize URL, validates in callback handler (400 on mismatch/missing). CSRF protection.
Fix 4 (Token exchange timeout): auth_setup.py token-exchange POST now has timeout=30 (was the only timeout-less request, carries client_secret + auth_code).
All 4 fixes have tests in tests/test_security_fixes.py (41 tests). Local only - no git commits made.
Review-loop APPROVED: 65/65 tests pass, ruff clean, no regressions. Review at .audit/50_fixes_review.md.

name: Metadata Feature (--metadata)
observations: CLI command: python tradestation_downloader.py --metadata (store_true flag, lazy import in run_download)
Fetches symbol details from GET /v3/marketdata/symbols/{symbols} (batches of 50) and quote snapshots from GET /v3/marketdata/quotes/{symbols} (batches of 100)
Derives session times from downloaded bar data (API doesn't provide them for futures): derive_session_times() per-weekday min/max, derive_sessions() contiguous blocks with gap threshold 15min
Session blocks: {start, end, duration_hours, spans_midnight}. Duration = (end-start+1)/60 or (1440-start+end+1)/60 for midnight-spanning. Around-the-clock = 00:00-23:59/24.0h.
Outputs JSON to stdout AND saves to data_dir/metadata.json

Output structure: {generated_at, data_dir, timezone: 'UTC', symbols: {SYMBOL: {symbol, api: {all SymbolDetail fields}, quote: {all Quote fields}, downloaded_data: {first_timestamp, last_timestamp, total_bars, exchange_timezone, session_times (local), session_times_utc, sessions (local), sessions_utc}}}}
Session times derived in BOTH UTC and exchange-local: convert_df_timezone(df, tz) converts each bar per-bar DST before deriving local sessions. UTC versions preserved as *_utc fields.
All new logic in tradestation/metadata.py (fetch_symbol_details, fetch_quote_snapshots, derive_session_times, derive_sessions, convert_df_timezone, get_exchange_timezone, run_metadata)
Added get_first_timestamp() to StorageBackend ABC + Daily/Monthly partitioned overrides (reads files[0] for efficiency)
Tests in tests/test_metadata.py (42 tests). Review at .audit/55_dst_fix_review.md.

name: Ponytail Coding Principle
observations: Forces the laziest solution that actually works: simplest, shortest, most minimal
Ladder: 1) Does this need to exist (YAGNI)? 2) Does it already exist in codebase? 3) Stdlib? 4) Native platform feature? 5) Already-installed dep? 6) One line? 7) Then write minimum code
Rules: no abstractions not explicitly requested, no new deps if avoidable, no unrequested boilerplate, deletion over addition, boring over clever, fewest files possible, shortest working diff wins

Not lazy about: understanding the problem (read fully + trace flow first), input validation at trust boundaries, error handling preventing data loss, security, accessibility, calibration real hardware needs
Non-trivial logic leaves ONE runnable check (assert-based demo or one small test file; no frameworks)
Applied throughout this session: minimal diffs, no new abstractions, deleted buggy convert_sessions_to_timezone instead of keeping it

name: CSV Export Feature (--export-csv)
observations: Customer requirement: CLI flag --export-csv exports already-downloaded parquet data to CSV format in a sibling directory 'plain_data' of the data_dir
When no -s/--symbols args passed: export all symbols found via storage.list_symbols()
When -s/--symbols args passed: those are the symbols to export; error if any has no data; user may drop the @ prefix (BO and @BO both work)
One CSV file per symbol (one parquet file -> one CSV file); CSV files MUST have extension *.txt (downstream importer software expects it)

CSV format per tests/example/ng_daily_20y_may2026.txt: header '"Date","Time","Open","High","Low","Close","Vol","OI"' (double-quoted header fields, capital first letters); data rows NOT quoted; date MM/DD/YYYY; time HH:MM 24h; separator comma

Mandatory CSV columns: Date, Time, Open, High, Low, Close. Volume added as 'Vol' if data present. OI (open interest) ignored - not present in our parquet data (no OI field in TradeStation bar API _COLUMN_MAP)
Parquet schema: columns are datetime (datetime64[ns], naive UTC, becomes DatetimeIndex named 'datetime' when datetime_index=True), open/high/low/close (float), volume (numeric). No OI column.

StorageBackend ABC already provides list_symbols() and load(symbol) for all three backends (single/daily/monthly) - NO new storage code needed. load() returns df with datetime as index when datetime_index=True; normalize via df.reset_index(names=['datetime']).

Integration mirrors --metadata feature exactly: new tradestation/csv_export.py module with run_export_csv(config_path, symbols=None) -> int; --export-csv store_true flag in cli.py after --metadata block; lazy import branch in run_download() after args.metadata branch

Bootstrap sequence (copy from metadata.py lines 229-253): load_config -> detect_storage_format(data_dir) with fallback to config.storage_format -> create_storage(storage_format, data_dir, compression=config.compression.value, datetime_index=config.datetime_index)
Output path: data_dir.parent / 'plain_data' / f'{symbol}.txt' (sibling of data_dir). Filename keeps @ prefix to match on-disk naming (e.g. @ES.txt) unless customer says otherwise.

Header quoting: pandas to_csv default (QUOTE_MINIMAL) won't quote all header fields. Simplest fix: write header line manually as '"Date","Time","Open","High","Low","Close","Vol"\n' then df.to_csv(path, mode='a', header=False, index=False, ...).
validate_symbol() in models.py MUST be called on user-supplied -s/--symbols args (path-traversal guard) BEFORE lookup against storage.list_symbols().
pandas and pyarrow already deps in pyproject.toml - NO new dependency needed for CSV export.

Tests: python -m pytest tests/ -o addopts="" ; Lint: python -m ruff check. Test pattern from tests/test_metadata.py: call run_export_csv directly, mock tradestation.csv_export.load_config, use temp_data_dir fixture, instantiate SingleFileStorage(temp_data_dir).save(symbol, df) to create sample parquet.
Research report at .pm_research/csv_export_research.md

IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-02: New module tradestation/csv_export.py with run_export_csv(config_path, symbols=None) -> int. CLI flag --export-csv wired in cli.py (mirrors --metadata pattern: store_true flag + lazy import branch in run_download).

Tests: tests/test_csv_export.py (14 tests) - format correctness, all-symbols export, specific-symbols export, @-prefix normalization (BO and @BO both work), missing-symbol error (exit 1), empty data dir, path traversal rejection (ValueError from validate_symbol), output directory location (sibling plain_data), DatetimeIndex handling, all 3 storage backends parametrized, CRLF line endings, datetime_index=False path.

Verification: 121/121 tests pass (14 new + 107 existing), ruff clean on touched files, live end-to-end CLI smoke test confirmed correct CSV format matching tests/example/ng_daily_20y_may2026.txt (double-quoted header, unquoted data, MM/DD/YYYY dates, HH:MM times, uniform CRLF).

Review-loop: 2 rounds. Round 1 DISAPPROVE (1 CRITICAL: mixed line endings on Windows - header CRLF via write_text, data LF via to_csv; example file is uniform CRLF). Round 2 APPROVE after fix: open file once with newline='' and write header+data with explicit \r\n.

Known limitation (NON-CRITICAL, not in spec): plain_data directory is not pruned before export - stale .txt files from prior runs with different symbol sets remain. Spec only requires 'one CSV file per symbol' for exported symbols, not directory pruning. Add pruning if user wants clean re-exports.

IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-04: Downloader now captures UpVolume, DownVolume, UpTicks, DownTicks from TradeStation API (previously silently discarded). Added to _COLUMN_MAP and _OUTPUT_COLUMNS in downloader.py. volume (TotalVolume) is KEPT for backward compat.

Parquet schema updated: columns are now datetime, open, high, low, close, volume, up_volume, down_volume, up_ticks, down_ticks. Old parquet files only have the first 6 columns (no up/down). New downloads have all 10.

CSV export updated: when up_volume AND down_volume are present, outputs Up, Down columns (and Upticks, Downticks if both tick columns present) instead of Vol. Falls back to Vol for old data with only volume column. Backward compatible.

API returns 18 fields per bar: High, Low, Open, Close, TimeStamp, TotalVolume (string), DownTicks, DownVolume, OpenInterest (string), IsRealtime, IsEndOfHistory, TotalTicks, UnchangedTicks, UnchangedVolume, UpTicks, UpVolume, Epoch, BarStatus. Downloader now captures 10 (was 6). Still discards: OpenInterest, TotalTicks, UnchangedTicks, UnchangedVolume, IsRealtime, IsEndOfHistory, Epoch, BarStatus.
Verified relationship: UpVolume + DownVolume + UnchangedVolume == TotalVolume (UnchangedVolume is 0 in observed samples). UpTicks + DownTicks + UnchangedTicks == TotalTicks.
Tests: tests/test_downloader_volume_fields.py (6 tests), tests/test_csv_export_up_down.py (7 tests). Full suite: 134 passed. Ruff clean. Live API call confirmed all 4 new fields captured correctly.
Review-loop: 1 round, APPROVE. All findings NON-CRITICAL (SIM113 lint fix bundled in downloader.py is behavior-preserving; no integrity check in CSV export by design).

name: Parquet Schema
observations: TradeStation Downloader parquet columns: datetime, open, high, low, close, volume (lowercase). No OI column.
datetime column is datetime64[ns], naive UTC (timezone stripped in downloader.py _bars_to_dataframe lines 307-309).

When datetime_index=True (default), parquet stores datetime as DatetimeIndex named 'datetime' (not a column); symbol folder/file gets _index_1 suffix. Loaded df has DatetimeIndex, need df.reset_index(names=['datetime']) to get column back.
open/high/low/close are float (via pd.to_numeric); volume is numeric (float64 after coercion).
Source: tradestation/downloader.py _COLUMN_MAP (lines 24-32) and _OUTPUT_COLUMNS; storage.py _prepare_dataframe (lines 17-38) enforces schema on write/load.

UPDATED 2026-08-04: Parquet columns are now datetime, open, high, low, close, volume, up_volume, down_volume, up_ticks, down_ticks (10 columns). Old parquet files only have the first 6 (datetime, open, high, low, close, volume). New downloads have all 10.
up_volume, down_volume, up_ticks, down_ticks are int (API returns them as ints, pd.to_numeric for safety). volume is string from API, converted to numeric.
Source: tradestation/downloader.py _COLUMN_MAP (lines 24-35) and _OUTPUT_COLUMNS (line 36).

name: Target CSV Format (TradeStation Importer)
observations: Example file: tests/example/ng_daily_20y_may2026.txt (5044 lines, daily-bar sample; repo downloads 1-min bars but format is the same target).
Header: "Date","Time","Open","High","Low","Close","Vol","OI" - ALL header fields double-quoted, comma-separated, capital first letters.
Data rows: NOT quoted, comma-separated. Date as MM/DD/YYYY (e.g. 05/15/2006). Time as HH:MM 24-hour (e.g. 17:00).
Column order: Date, Time, Open, High, Low, Close, Vol, OI.
Volume column labeled 'Vol' (not 'Volume'), plain integers. OI column labeled 'OI', plain integers (NOT available in our parquet data - must be omitted).
File extension is .txt (NOT .csv) - required by downstream importer software.
